method: Reconstructed the three years from the official dated English curriculum and individual study-guide entries. Rechecked the choice order, methods preparation and thesis entry before reconsidering the frozen comparison and workbook-backed content.
findings: The English catalogue shows eight credited first-year units worth 60 EC. Uncredited academic writing sits alongside Media Research, with a separate literacy test and tutoring. The English public page lists Film Studies first; the guide confirms three distinct 12 EC choice groups. The Film route gives Film Practices in blocks 1–2, Film Analysis in blocks 2–3 and Advanced Topics: Film in blocks 5–6. The common courses provide 24 EC and place the two philosophy units consecutively.

Positive binding study advice applies to the Film courses. First-year Media Aesthetics supports Film Analysis and Practices, and it precedes Advanced Topics with Media Theory and Media Research. The third year leaves 42 EC open and assigns 18 EC to one semester of seminar and thesis. The course entry exempts Film or Television Practices from prior completion for thesis entry, with the selected practice course still required for graduation.

Media & the Environment and From T.V. to TikTok deepen the broad media history option. The film option has a distinct visual storytelling emphasis in adaptation, museums, visual heritage and rhetoric. Television and digital representation, audience research methods and public discourse underpin the third option. Modern Sociology moves to a verified term and the unsupported Market Research prerequisite disappears with that substitution. Pairwise changes are 45, 60 and 67.5 EC each way.

Five specific overlaps survive source comparison: audiovisual form, historical media change, documentary practice, film analysis and qualitative research design. Verified 17 external component titles, all 36 selected titles and descriptions, eight component and cell note references, three concepts, limitations and official sources. The optional UCR research item remains separate from the schedule and from the compulsory UvA thesis.
